findings.note: `fsm gate <name>` returns exit 1 for a failing gate while reporting status "OK" and no top-level `code` (run.go:698, run.go:702). The driver contract in AgentPrompt states only two exit-1 shapes: "exit 1 with GATE_FAILED" and "exit 1 with ERR_*" (internal/fsm/cli/prompt.go:11-12). An agent following that contract literally on a `fsm gate` invocation finds neither, and must know to look inside env["gate"]["code"] instead. Either document the diagnostic subcommand's exit-1 shape or emit GATE_FAILED.

findings.note: `--calibration` is silently ignored by standalone `fsm judge` (no --run). run.go:763 hard-codes calibration=false into judge.Preflight, whereas the --run path reads it from the snapshot (run.go:757). --calibration parses as a valid bool flag for every subcommand (boolFlags, run.go:78) and AgentPrompt lists it as an agent-satisfiable knob, so a caller passing it to an unaudited judge call gets a silently different pre-flight than they asked for. Reject it, or honour it.

findings.note: parseArgs cannot express a flag value that begins with "--": run.go:101-103 treats any next token starting with "--" as a missing value and errors. This makes some legitimate inputs unrepresentable, e.g. `--var K=--v` is fine but `--data --x` or a run/model/effort value with a leading dash is not. There is no `--` end-of-flags escape. Low impact today because no current value legitimately starts with two dashes, but it is a latent usability trap with a confusing error message ("missing value for --data").

evidence.note: returns "missing value" whenever the next token has the -- prefix

findings.note: Both new rollback tests can pass while proving nothing. They make docs/metareview/reviews mode 0555 and then `t.Skip("the review body unexpectedly succeeded; nothing proved")` if Create succeeds — so the rollback assertion is skipped rather than failed. Two ways it goes vacuous silently: running as root (0555 does not block root writes), and any future change that makes Create tolerate an unwritable review directory. A skip reports green in CI. Prefer injecting the post-pack failure deterministically (a seam that fails the review body) so the rollback assertion cannot be skipped.

findings.note: The two new .calibration.golden files pin, by design, that calibration mode drops the nonce fence around untrusted content: RenderPrompt sets `fence = false` when calibration (internal/fsm/judge/prompts.go:197), so the diff and the finding text are interpolated raw. The goldens make this explicit and reassuring on one axis — the injected `{{1}}`, `}}`, `<<<END-0123456789abcdef` and a literal `{diff}` inside the diff payload are all reproduced verbatim, confirming format() is genuinely single-pass and does not rescan slot values — but they also show attacker-controlled diff content sitting unfenced in the prompt, including a forged `<<<END-` sentinel. This is the intended calibration-parity behaviour with the reference harness rather than a defect, and calibration is opt-in, but it deserves a comment in the golden or the template noting that calibration prompts are deliberately unfenced and must not be used to judge untrusted input.
